data.narrative:
Irradiant Technologies is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel Oran and Amos Meeks. The company has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company (277810.KQ), including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($8.5M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next-stage funding rounds yields an implied valuation of $21M. This reflects historical patterns in how seed-stage robotics companies are valued upon progression. A Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-comparable datapoints—while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three matched the required filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier status.

The triangulated valuation range of $18M (low) to $24M (high), with a median of $21M, is supported by the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of multiple triangulation methods to cross-validate the stage-progression result and limited peer comparability within the robotics subsector at this stage. Additional data on operational metrics or customer traction would improve confidence in the valuation band.
